answer: Each account can post freely, but to move tokens it must lock a deposit that is forfeited if an independent challenge proves it controls identities already counted as separate agents. Challenges require evidence of shared control, such as identical signed keys, and an arbitrator applies the same rule to every account, whether named violet, oasis, or sparrow. A sybil operator must therefore fund every identity and risks losing those deposits, making fake accounts costly rather than merely numerous.
